beats.text: As soon as he left, an old sage with an umbrella and a water pot came to the hut, asking for alms.
The trees stopped moving. The river grew still. Even the wind was afraid.
Sita saw nothing wrong with the old man. She offered him food and water from inside the line, as later tellings say.
He insisted she come out. 'A holy man cannot take alms from behind a line.' She stepped over the line.
The sage turned into Ravana, king of Lanka, his ten heads blazing with anger.
'Be my queen,' he said, 'and rule golden Lanka.' Sita refused. 'You are a jackal. Rama is a lion.'
He seized her and flew into the sky in his golden chariot.
'Tell Rama!' she cried to the trees, the river and the deer. Sita's cries echoed across the forest.
